problems.title: Monsoon Inundation & Flash Floodwater Ingress at Govt Middle School Bundu
problems.description: During every monsoon downpour, flash flood runoff from the nearby Subarnarekha tributary surges directly into the Government Middle School Bundu campus. Classrooms and the kitchen shed submerge in 2.5 feet of stagnant muddy water. School operations halt for 18-22 instructional days each year, posing acute dengue and electrical hazards to 500 tribal boys and girls.

location.landmark: Near Bundu Block Development Office & Subarnarekha Tributary

evidence.caption: Classroom corridor submerged under 2.5 feet of flash stream runoff
Mid-day meal ration store inundated by muddy water ingress

aiAnalysis.summary: Critical flash monsoon runoff ingress at Govt Middle School Bundu campus. Inundates classrooms to 2.5 ft, cutting off 500 students and halting mid-day meal operations.
aiAnalysis.possibleGovernmentDepartment: Department of School Education & Literacy / Water Resources Dept Jharkhand
aiAnalysis.rootCause: Absence of graded stormwater bypass channel coupled with low-lying compound grading directly aligned with the natural micro-watershed tributary discharge.
aiAnalysis.affectedPopulation: 500 enrolled tribal primary/middle students, 14 school staff, and neighboring 120 households
aiAnalysis.locationExpertise: Ranchi district Subarnarekha upper catchment drainage profile
aiAnalysis.solutionDomain: Integrated IoT ultrasonic hydrological telemetry, automated solar cloud early-warning alarm node, and civil retention-bypass drainage conduits.
aiAnalysis.expectedOutcome: Zero school closure days, 75% reduction in floodwater ingress events (from 12/yr to 3/yr during peak cloudbursts), and real-time SMS/siren alerts 45 minutes prior to flood surge.

Directly affects 500 tribal children, halting mid-day meal & 18 instruction days/yr

Multiple photographic proof documents school building inundated to 2.5 feet
